item.title: Pat McAfee has put more than $6 million of his own money into GameDay prizes and charity
item.description: An LSU student named Bruce had a chance at a million-dollar reward during a broadcast sponsored by Pat McAfee and Home Depot. Selected randomly from the crowd, he attempted a 33-yard field goal twice but unfortunately missed both shots. This challenge comes on the heels of prior seasons where students successfully claimed large cash prizes along with donations to charity.

item.title: In 2014, a tech entrepreneur bought a 1,100-acre Sonoma ranch for $12 million and spent...
item.description: A remarkable 1,100-acre estate on Sonoma Mountain has been sold for an astounding $38.5 million. Entrepreneurs Mark and Debra Leslie have converted this once undeveloped land into a self-sustaining retreat, pouring in $33 million for environmental restoration and diverse farming infrastructures. The property boasts a contemporary main residence with breathtaking views, showcasing the growing interest in secluded, off-grid homes in coastal California.

item.title: In 1997, Texas mixed discarded roofing shingles into two 1,000-foot Highway 31 test sections
item.description: Engineers in Texas have made groundbreaking progress by recycling discarded roofing shingles into robust road surfaces. After extensive testing, these innovative materials showed they could match the performance of conventional asphalt, enduring significant traffic wear. The success of this pilot program also spurred the implementation of state-wide regulations that promote the use of recycled shingles in highway construction, leading to both cost savings and conservation of natural resources.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A company bought 7,500 acres of England for £8.5 million to create ‘Britain’s Yellowstone'
item.description: A pioneering nature restoration firm has acquired Emblehope Moor to embark on a significant rewilding initiative. This visionary endeavor seeks to establish a thriving wildlife haven in northern England, while ensuring investors receive returns on their contributions prior to the land transfer. The project focuses on revitalizing peatlands and eliminating invasive tree species, all while valuing and utilizing local expertise for effective rewilding practices.

item.title: Meet the US’ first professional Santa with Down syndrome
item.description: Meet Bradley Carlisle, a groundbreaking figure as the first professional Santa Claus with Down syndrome. After graduating from a performer school and being inducted into the International Santa Claus Hall of Fame, Carlisle conquered his childhood fears related to Santa. Encouraged by his mother and an association's outreach, he stepped into this beloved role. His journey underlines the significance of inclusivity and spotlights his remarkable abilities.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Ultra-rich pay $650,000 for Martha’s Vineyard 'beach keys'
item.description: Exclusive access to beaches on Martha's Vineyard is proving to be a hot commodity, with keys selling for exorbitant amounts—often in the hundreds of thousands. These keys offer private shorelines away from the crowded tourist spots, appealing to affluent buyers. The rising demand pushes prices higher, leaving locals and seasonal renters feeling alienated and resentful over their dwindling access to the island’s natural beauty.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Michèle Mouton's father told her to prove herself or quit rallying; she became the ‘fastest woman alive’
item.description: Michèle Mouton broke through the male-dominated world of rally racing, becoming the first woman to claim victory in a World Rally Championship event. Her impressive skill nearly earned her the world title in 1982, showcasing her talent. Mouton also conquered the famed Pikes Peak International Hill Climb. Her groundbreaking career inspired future female motorsport participants and led her to advocate for women's roles in racing through the FIA commission.

item.title: After a 25-acre Lake Erie wetland was reconnected, sonar recorded 3.44 million fish detections
item.description: A rejuvenated wetland at Lake Erie witnessed an influx of aquatic wildlife thanks to its reconnection. High-resolution sonar has captured a staggering 3.4 million fish movements entering and exiting this newly transformed habitat. This research reveals valuable insights into how aquatic species engage with restored coastal ecosystems, as fish showcased varied activity throughout both day and night, influencing management strategies for restoring Great Lakes wetlands.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: In 2024, Arizona used foam made from 100% recycled glass at 19 sites while...
item.description: In a groundbreaking interstate expansion project in Arizona, engineers harnessed recycled glass aggregate as a revolutionary structural fill. This eco-friendly innovation not only provided lightweight support for drainage culverts but also showcased impressive compressive strength. Utilizing foam glass from recycled bottles minimized the need for expensive culvert replacements and significantly cut down on construction delays, ultimately transforming waste into vital infrastructure enhancements.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Hulk Hogan’s Florida mansion gets another $1M price cut, now listed at $6.9M after three reductions
item.description: Hulk Hogan’s Clearwater Beach mansion has received another $1 million price cut and is now listed for $6.9 million. The wrestler’s five-bedroom waterfront home was initially listed for $10.98 million after his death. Hogan bought the property for $3.33 million in 2012, while his neighbouring property was purchased for $1.6 million four years later.

item.title: US war veteran's home threatened by Elon Musk's AI data centre in Tennessee
item.description: Residents in Memphis are grappling with the effects of a massive artificial intelligence data center that has recently opened its doors. The surge in energy consumption has led to soaring utility bills for local families, casting a shadow on community wellbeing. Amidst growing noise pollution and escalating living costs, citizens are voicing concerns about the sustainability of such rapid technological advancements and their impact on daily life.

item.title: Jaguar Land Rover may cut 4,000 jobs as Tata-owned carmaker targets £1.7bn savings after cyberattack
item.description: Jaguar Land Rover may cut up to 4,000 jobs as the Tata-owned carmaker targets £1.7bn in savings over two years and seeks to lower its break-even point to 300,000 vehicles. The move comes a year after a major cyberattack disrupted production and could put further pressure on Andy Burnham’s pledge to reindustrialise Britain.
